canonical_topic: Individual rate of return (IRR) vs. market interest rate
definition: An individual's expected rate of return on their own investments is their individual rate of return (IRR); the interest rate is the aggregate consensus of all market participants' IRRs.
core_idea: Interest rates observed in the market are essentially a collective aggregation of individual investors' expected returns, used as the benchmark for time-value-of-money comparisons.
key_points: IRR is personal/individual — it reflects one investor's own expected return from their investment opportunities.
The market interest rate emerges as the consensus across all participants' individual rates of return.
relationships: IRR feeds into the broader market interest rate, which is then used generally as the time-value-of-money benchmark.
trading_implications: A trader's personal discount rate (IRR) may differ from the quoted market interest rate, affecting how they individually value future cash flows relative to the broader market.
caveats: Treating 'interest rate' and 'individual rate of return' as synonyms; the former is a market consensus, the latter is specific to one participant.
